newsitem.title: CANADA: Finning sees another record year in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Finning sees another record year in 1997.

text.p: Heavy equipment dealer Finning International Inc, which has had 63 years of uninterrupted earnings growth, said Monday it expects to achieve record revenues and earnings again in 1997.
Finning, which claims to be the world's biggest dealer of Caterpillar Inc equipment, earlier reported a rise in second-quarter net operating earnings to a record C$0.29 a share from C$0.23.
"With this pace of activity, we are on our way to setting record revenue and earnings again in 1997," chief executive Jim Shephard said.
Finning earned C$1.03 a share in 1996 on a net operating basis after the effect of a stock split and has earned C$0.56 a share in the first half of 1997 on the same basis.
"Our Canadian operations have done well in the first six months of this year despite the weakness in the forestry sector. Chile, as expected, continues its strong performance," Shephard said.

Finning said it expects to make an announcement in the "near future" on its discussions with Unilever Plc for the purchase of the Caterpillar dealership in the north, east and southeast regions of England, currently held by Unilever's subsidiary, H. Leverton Ltd.
The acquisition, announced last summer, had been expected to close earlier this year but has been delayed because it hinged on parallel moves by Unilever to restructure its operations.
The two companies have signed a confidentiality agreement that bars Finning from releasing further details on the talks.
The deal would add about C$500 million a year to Finning's revenues.
